findings.title: inflightCreate is shared across provisional windows: a send in a SECOND new-chat window lands in the FIRST window's session
findings.failure_scenario: User taps New (provisional A, pseudo storedId new:x) and sends; sendPrompt -> ensureSession starts runNewChat(A) and sets the module-global inflightCreate. While that session.create RPC is still in flight (slow/remote gateway), the user taps New again (provisional B becomes active) and sends. sendPrompt sees ps.provisional (B) and calls ensureSession(), which returns `await inflightCreate` — A's session id. The message typed into chat B is submitted to chat A and the user bubble is grafted onto A's transcript (patchSession(sid=A)), while the user keeps looking at B. activeLiveId() (lines 1247-1250) has the same defect, so slash-completion and option-sheet RPCs can also hit the wrong window's session.
evidence: app/src/lib/chat.ts:1184 — `if (inflightCreate) return await inflightCreate` without checking that the in-flight create belongs to the CURRENT provisional window
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1187-1191 — inflightCreate is a single module-global; only `inflightCreate === p` clears it
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1755-1760 — sendPrompt: `if (ps?.provisional) { sid = await ensureSession() }` — resolves the ACTIVE window's create, not the pinned one
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1271-1302 — newChat() is fully local; a second tap mints a second provisional while the first create is still in flight
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1247-1250 — activeLiveId: same unconditional `return await inflightCreate`
reproduction_steps: 1. Tap the New-chat button; immediately type a message and send (session.create now in flight).
2. While the create is still pending (easy on a slow link), tap New again — screen shows a fresh empty chat.
3. Type a second message and send.
4. Observe: the second message's user bubble appears in chat 1 (switch to it via the drawer); chat 2 never receives it.
findings.suggested_remediation: Key the in-flight create to its provisional window (e.g. Map<tempId, Promise<string>>), and in ensureSession/activeLiveId only await the promise for the SAME tempId; otherwise start a new runNewChat for the current window.
findings.limitations: Timing-dependent: requires the second send while the first create RPC is unsettled; could not run the app (read-only audit).

findings.title: Pinned send to a provisional chat resolves ensureSession() against the ACTIVE chat — offline text composed in a new-chat window is delivered to whichever chat is open at flush time
findings.failure_scenario: User composes a message in a provisional new-chat window offline; sendPrompt's resolution-phase catch enqueues it to the outbox pinned to t0.storedId — which for a provisional window is the pseudo id `new:…` (line 1799). On reconnect, flushOutbox finds the provisional entry by storedId and calls sendPrompt(item.text, { session: tempKey }) (line 834). sendPrompt's `ps?.provisional` branch calls `ensureSession()` with no argument, which resolves/creates the ACTIVE session — if the user has since switched to chat C, the message is submitted to chat C, violating the pinned-delivery invariant the file documents for BUG-008.
evidence: app/src/lib/chat.ts:1799 — `enqueueOffline(text, t0?.storedId ?? '')` — t0 can be the provisional entry, so the outbox item's storedId is a `new:…` pseudo id
app/src/lib/chat.ts:832-834 — flushOutbox resolves `find(s => s.storedId === item.storedId)?.id` and pins the send to it (the provisional temp key)
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1757-1760 — `if (ps?.provisional) { sid = await ensureSession() }` — ensureSession reads activeSession.get(), ignoring `pinned` entirely
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1176-1192 — ensureSession resolves whatever window is currently active, or creates one
reproduction_steps: 1. Go offline (airplane mode). Tap New, type a message, send — it fails and is parked in the outbox pinned to the `new:` pseudo id.
2. Stay on the provisional window (do not let the create succeed) and switch to another chat, then reconnect with the provisional still present.
3. flushOutbox runs on the online edge (app/(tabs)/chat.tsx:276-286).
4. The message is submitted to the currently active session, not the chat it was composed in.
findings.suggested_remediation: In sendPrompt's provisional branch, if `pinned` is set, await the create for THAT window (pass tempId through, per A-01's keyed map); otherwise treat a pseudo-pinned outbox item as unpinned-with-target rather than falling back to the active chat.
findings.limitations: Requires the provisional window to still exist at flush time; otherwise resumeShared('new:…') fails and the item is (correctly) dropped or retried.

findings.title: BUG-036 (timeout double-submit) is still unfixed and flushOutbox automates the duplicate: a timed-out prompt.submit is re-sent on the next flush
findings.failure_scenario: prompt.submit has no idempotency key and the channel's 120s timeout only rejects the client-side promise — the server may have received and started the turn. sendPrompt's catch marks the user row failed and rethrows; when the send came from flushOutbox, its catch re-enqueues the item (text not re-enqueued by sendPrompt's submit-phase path), so the NEXT flush (next reconnect edge) submits the same text again while the first turn is still running/finished — duplicate turn, duplicate reply, double tool spend. Same for a user tapping retry on the failed row.
evidence: app/src/protocol/json-rpc-channel.ts:252-258 — timeout deletes the pending call and rejects; the frame was already sent, no cancellation
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1847-1863 — prompt.submit has no dedupe/idempotency field; retry only on session-not-found
app/src/lib/chat.ts:852-862 — flushOutbox catch re-enqueues the item because sendPrompt's submit-phase failure did not re-enqueue it
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1896-1915 — retryMessage resubmits the same text with no server-side dedupe
reproduction_steps: 1. Send a prompt against a loaded gateway where prompt.submit acks slower than 120s (or throttle the link).
2. Request times out; row shows failed.
3. The server actually received the submit and runs the turn.
4. Tap retry (or trigger any reconnect flush with the item still in the outbox): the same prompt runs twice.
findings.suggested_remediation: Client half: carry a client-generated submit id in prompt.submit params and skip resubmission when the same id was already acked/seen; tracker's note stands that the real fix is server-side dedupe.

findings.title: BUG-086 confirmed still open in this commit: server requests for untracked sessions are filed under a key pendingRequest can never match — unanswerable, and no dot anywhere
findings.failure_scenario: An approval/clarify arrives for a session this app instance never tracked (automation/CLI/another device). onServerRequestMessage's rebind (storedIdFor -> sessionsById scan) finds nothing, so the request is filed under a live id with no sessionsById entry. pendingRequest (computed over activeSession) can never equal that key, so no question card renders on any screen; pendingStoredIds maps it through map[liveId]?.storedId which is undefined, so the row gets no amber dot. The request sits until the backend deadline — matches the tracker's open BUG-086 exactly.
evidence: app/src/lib/chat.ts:2096-2100 — rebind only succeeds when a tracked entry shares the stored id; otherwise sessionId stays untracked
app/src/lib/chat.ts:2110-2134 — withPending files the item regardless of whether sessionsById has the key
app/src/lib/chat.ts:232-236 — pendingRequest = pendingBySession[activeSession]; an untracked key never equals activeSession
app/src/lib/chat.ts:255-264 — pendingStoredIds drops entries whose live id has no map entry (stored = undefined, filtered)
reproduction_steps: 1. Start a long-running automation/CLI session on the machine (not from the phone).
2. Let it raise an approval question.
3. Phone receives the server request; no card, no dot, and the question cannot be answered from the phone until the backend deadline.
findings.suggested_remediation: Materialize a minimal sessionsById entry (or a side-map keyed by stored id) for untracked-request sessions so pendingRequest/pendingStoredIds can surface and answer them, mirroring the sessionRows path.

findings.title: steerRun falls through to session.steer on any unrecognized session.redirect status, potentially applying the text twice
findings.failure_scenario: steerRun treats only 'redirected'/'queued' as success. If session.redirect resolves with any other status (new server version, partial application, or a shape drift), the code assumes the redirect did nothing and also calls session.steer with the same text. If the redirect actually applied the message server-side, the user's steer is processed twice (two user messages / two agent iterations).
evidence: app/src/lib/chat.ts:1958-1965 — only 'redirected'|'queued' short-circuits; every other resolved value falls through
app/src/lib/chat.ts:1968 — fallback `await rpc('session.steer', …)` runs unconditionally after the fall-through
reproduction_steps: 1. Send a steer while a turn runs against a gateway whose session.redirect returns an unexpected status value.
2. If the redirect applied the text, session.steer applies it again — visible as a duplicated user steer in the transcript.
findings.suggested_remediation: Whitelist the statuses that mean 'not applied' before falling back, or log-and-return on unknown statuses instead of double-sending.
findings.limitations: Server-side status vocabulary not verified (Python side out of scope); severity depends entirely on whether unknown statuses can co-occur with an applied redirect.

findings.title: isKnownSlashCommand returns true whenever the catalog is empty, so offline/boot any '/…' text is routed to the command pipeline and answered with 'Command failed' instead of being sent as a message
findings.failure_scenario: Before loadCatalog() succeeds (cold boot, offline, gateway error), commandCatalog is {} and isKnownSlashCommand short-circuits to true for ANY leading-slash text. Chat.send() then routes e.g. '/usr/bin/env — what's in there?' into runSlash -> activeLiveId (may force a session create while offline -> throws) -> runCommand -> RPC failure -> the composer text is restored but the user gets a 'Command failed' alert and the message is never sent, contrary to BUG-042's stated intent that unknown slash-text is a normal message.
evidence: app/src/lib/slash.ts:266-267 — `const catalog = commandCatalog.get(); if (Object.keys(catalog).length === 0) return true`
app/app/(tabs)/chat.tsx:620-623 — send() dispatches to runSlash when isKnownSlashCommand(text)
app/app/(tabs)/chat.tsx:425-426,456-461 — runSlash awaits activeLiveId()/runCommand and on failure alerts 'Command failed' instead of sending the text as a turn
reproduction_steps: 1. Fresh install or offline start (catalog never loaded).
2. Type '/etc/hosts — summarize this' and tap send.
3. Instead of the message being sent (or queued), an error alert appears and nothing is delivered.
findings.suggested_remediation: Only default-to-true when a catalog load has actually been attempted and the gateway confirmed an empty catalog; otherwise return false (treat as a message) when offline/catalog-empty.

findings.title: migrateV1Transcript's interim-key early return skips the legacy live-keyed v1 cleanup, stranding those blobs in AsyncStorage
findings.failure_scenario: When the interim stored-keyed `.v1` blob exists, the function copies it to v2 and returns BEFORE the loop at line 645 that removes every legacy live-keyed `.v1` transcript mapped to this stored id. Those blobs (up to 300 messages each, several vintages per chat) stay in AsyncStorage indefinitely for live chats; they are only swept on chat deletion or a backend-identity purge.
evidence: app/src/lib/chat.ts:624-629 — `if (interim) { …; return interim }` precedes the cleanup
app/src/lib/chat.ts:637-645 — legacy live-keyed removal loop only runs on the non-interim path
reproduction_steps: 1. Upgrade from a build that wrote both interim stored-keyed v1 and legacy live-keyed v1 blobs for the same chat.
2. Open the chat (v2 hydrates via the interim path).
3. Inspect AsyncStorage: the old hermes.transcript.<liveId>.v1 keys remain.
findings.suggested_remediation: Run the legacy live-keyed removal loop before the interim early return (it is read-only work already computed above).

findings.title: Batch clarify Send submits without requiring an answer per question — unanswered qids are silently omitted from the answers map
findings.failure_scenario: The batch clarify card's Send button is always enabled (chat.tsx:1245-1250). respondClarifyBatch forwards batchAnswers verbatim; questions the user never answered (no choice tapped, empty free-text) are simply missing qids in { answers }. If the backend applies only the provided answers, those questions stay blocking or get retried; the user gets no indication that a question went back unanswered. There is also no client-side guard against submitting a completely empty map.
evidence: app/app/(tabs)/chat.tsx:1245-1250 — Send button with no validation of batchAnswers coverage
app/src/lib/chat.ts:2064-2070 — `answer(req.id, { answers })` sends the map as-is; no per-qid completeness check
reproduction_steps: 1. Trigger a multi-question clarify (questions array with 2+ entries, at least one free-text).
2. Answer only the first question and tap Send.
3. The answers frame contains a single qid; the other question's fate depends entirely on backend behavior.
findings.suggested_remediation: Require every qid to have a non-empty answer before enabling Send (or send explicit empty answers per qid, whichever the v7 contract specifies).
findings.limitations: Backend tolerance for partial answers not verified (server side out of scope).
